<reason>Both sides were disciplined, format-compliant (clear A1:/A2: labels, tight questions) and avoided fake sourcing. B correctly identified that the motion needs only "hardness," not uniqueness, which blunted A's slippery-slope opening — that was B's best structural move. But over the full exchange A built the more complete affirmative reason to vote: (i) carbon as a quantity harm, so justification tracks the margin; (ii) the counterfactual point that the forgone ticket funds a yacht, not malaria nets; (iii) the cadence-to-cheaper-launch mechanism that gives space tourism a public payoff no other luxury has; and (iv) the "no ledger" argument that nobody's allocation grows if the ticket is refused. B's central assertion — that a ticket "spends scarce atmospheric room" taken from the worst-off — was repeatedly asserted but never squarely defended against that no-ledger pressure beyond a brief externality gesture. A also converted B's own concessions into damage: "both can be hard" [B4.6/B5.5] let A show the principle is really about luxury in general, and B's answer that cleaning the soot leaves the case intact let A land the "verdict immune to evidence" hit alongside the unnameable-threshold reply. B's reductio ("if no tonne wrecks a coastline, every luxury tonne is easy whenever coal is bigger") was genuinely good and kept the debate close, and "if the instruments matter, buy the instruments" was memorable, but A's answer that launch capability is not purchasable apart from cadence went largely unmet, and B's closing leaned on repeated slogans rather than new resolution. B also carried a small execution cost from the clipped first rebuttal. Narrow but real edge to A on weighing and comparative payoff.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's ivory-analogy dismantling: distinguishing intrinsic per-transaction harm from aggregate quantity harm, then showing that on PRO's own comparative test (privilege, intensity, no necessity) yachts and private jets are outclassed — combined with the follow-up that PRO's verdict moves no tonne and no dollar, which B answered only with "a verdict need not write a cheque."</best_rebuttal>
